QF.id: Cat III AIF Fees and Performance_23

question.text: If the High-Water Mark of an open-ended Cat III AIF is consistently rising, it signals:

answer.text: Poor fund performance and loss of investor trust
Superior past/present performance and a good indicator for future returns

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that a consistently rising HWM for an open-ended Category III AIF denotes superior past and present performance and can serve as a good indicator of future estimated returns for the scheme. The Trap: A static or declining HWM signals weaker performance; HWM movement is not a measure of regulatory compliance or leverage usage. Note: Per workbook pages 168 and 174.
